transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Ysolde 3 FP, Aldous 3 FP, Morwen 3 FP, Mire 3 FP. Face-up: Rising Floodwaters [H-03], Hive-Touched Pack [T-01].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain comes down in grey sheets over the Ashwater Causeway, the last dry road left in the Sallowmere. Ahead, the timber planking bows under black water that wasn't there yesterday, and behind you a plank cart lies overturned, its owner nowhere in sight — only a dropped hook-spear, and drag marks leading into the reeds. Something is moving out there, low and patient, pacing you along the flooded verge in a ragged line of shapes that used to be people. The causeway itself groans, planks vanishing into the flood a hundred yards ahead where the water has already claimed the road. You have to decide, now, whether to push forward across ground that may already be gone, or find another way before the pack closes the distance.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Not forward—we walk into the dark that way. The reedmere north, the shallow channels. Those things move like water itself, but they'll be slow and tangled in the growth. I know the way; I've taken it before when I needed disappearing.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps back from the causeway's edge, her weathered hands gripping the rope of her pack. Her eyes track the pack's movements with the same intensity she once used to read a crew's moods—low, predatory, moving in broken patterns through the reeds. She's survived this long by knowing when to push and when to slip sideways. She points north where the reeds grow thick and the channels wind tight.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The rain shows me a way. The pack hasn't gone east yet—the water there still speaks of older drownings, and the living things fear it. We cross there, if we're quick, and we might put distance between ourselves and their teeth.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous closes his eyes and lets the cold rain fall across his face, his fingers twitching slightly as he reads the water's patterns—the temperature shifts, the current's whisper, the echo of movements only a drowned man could know. The ghosts that cling to him shudder and point. When he opens his eyes again, they're sharp and certain, and he's looking not at the causeway ahead, but at the marshland beyond it, where the water runs differently.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Stand back! The Order holds this ground, and I will not let you pass.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen whirls to face the pack advancing along the flooded verge, planting herself firmly on the causeway. She calls upon her exorcist's will, speaking words of binding and warding meant to drive back the hive-touched, her hands raised in a gesture of command.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Keep eyes on those things behind us. I'm checking if there's ground ahead or if we're already cut off.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire moves to the edge of the causeway, eyes narrowed against the rain. She studies the flooded section ahead where the planking has vanished—tracing the waterline, calculating depth and current. How far does it actually extend? Is there a shallower passage along the verge, or does the road come back up beyond? Behind her, those low shapes in the reeds are getting closer. She needs to know if forward is even possible.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Not now. Keep your head, Mire. That's not Scarhook anymore—it's what ate him. And if I don't scout this ford, we all drown.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire refuses a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — create advantage with Notice: dice + - - + → Great (+4) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — attack with Will: dice - + - + → Great (+4) vs Poor (-1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (Scarhook taken out)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — overcome with Notice: dice 0 + 0 0 → Great (+4) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Morwen's warding cry cracks like a lightning strike over the water — Scarhook, or the thing that wore his face, seizes mid-lunge, claws inches from her throat, and folds backward into the flood without a sound. The rest of the pack scatters at the sight, hissing low, unwilling to close on a will that strong. In the same breath Aldous straightens from his rain-trance, pointing east where the drowned-old current runs wrong-way and untouched — a path the pack hasn't claimed, and won't dare follow. Mire, boots at the water's edge, calls back over her shoulder that the ford ahead is bad, but not impassable: she's found the shallow line along the old pilings, just visible under the churn. Between Morwen's blow and Aldous's reading, the way opens. You go east, feet finding solid wood beneath black water, the pack's cries falling away behind you into the rain — and somewhere ahead, through the grey, the crooked rooftops of Hollowmoot rise on their stilts.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The stilts of Hollowmoot rise out of the grey like the ribs of some beached animal, walkways slick and crowded with refugees pressed shoulder to shoulder under sagging awnings. At the causeway gate a Warden sergeant stands over a door freshly marked with a crossed ash sigil, torch unlit but ready, while a small crowd watches in tight, frightened silence. Before you've gone twenty paces past the gate, a woman splashes through the standing water to grab at your sleeves — soaked to the bone, eyes raw from crying, a fisherman's hook still clutched uselessly in one hand. She says her boy followed the swarm-song three nights ago, out past the causeway, out to the Drowned Temple's belltower, and she's begged every Warden and every pilgrim in Hollowmoot and been turned away by all of them. Behind her, the sergeant is already eyeing your party the way he eyes anyone who stops to listen too long.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Your boy—what's his name? Tell me everything you remember from that night. I've sailed waters where things call to people; I know what that song sounds like.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde stops walking and turns to face the woman fully, her weathered hands gentling on the hook-spear clutched there. She doesn't shrug the woman off or hurry past; instead, she settles into the patient attention that once made night-barge crew members trust her with their deepest fears—the weight that made her dangerous, the listening that made her necessary. She notices the Warden sergeant's gaze from across the flooded square but doesn't acknowledge it. Right now, this mother's raw-eyed desperation matters more than whatever the Order thinks it's watching for.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Your boy heard the swarm-song and went to the temple—I can read it in the rain that soaked you when he left, mother. Tell me his name, and I swear by the water that marks me: before the flood takes him, I'll bring him back or know the reason why.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous stops dead and turns to face the woman squarely, not pulling away from her grip on his sleeves. He meets her raw, desperate eyes without flinching. His fingers move subtly against the wet fabric of her clothes, reading the pattern of water and salt and time—the traces of a mother's anguish and a son's absence. When he speaks, his voice carries the certainty of someone who has already kept faith with the drowned. He doesn't glance at the sergeant watching from the gate.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I won't turn away. Tell me his name, what he looks like, how long the swarm-song has had him.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen strides back through the crowd to face the woman directly, the same will that turned back the hive-touched now bearing down on this moment. She meets Warden Sergeant Coale's gaze unflinching.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: How long was he under the song before he went? And has anything come back asking for him since?

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire stops when the woman grabs her sleeve, crouching to meet her eyes. She grips the woman's wrist gently—a warden's steadiness cutting through panic. The sergeant watches from his post, but she doesn't turn away. This is what wardens do, marked enemy or not.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: That's right. Orrin trials. And I'm still an exorcist. This woman's boy is hive-touched, out at the Drowned Temple, and I'm not turning away—the Order doesn't own my mercy.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: There—that grey cloak moving toward the gate. One of the Order's teeth just recognized my voice. So be it; I've been hunted before, and I'm not leaving this mother without an answer.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The mother's name comes out in a rush between sobs: Sera, and the boy is Tomas, nine years old, gone three nights now. She says the song took him slow — humming in his sleep, then walking toward it wide-eyed in daylight, then gone before dawn, following a sound none of the rest of them could hear. Ysolde's patient listening, Aldous's water-reading, Mire's steady grip and Morwen's flat refusal to look away all land on Sera at once, and something in her unclenches — for the first time in three days, someone believes her. But the price comes due as promised: across the square, the grey-cloaked figure who marked Ysolde's face doesn't approach, just watches, then turns and moves off toward the temple road with purpose, already carrying word. And Sergeant Coale, hearing Morwen name herself exorcist and swear an oath the Order itself would recognize, plants his unlit torch in the mud and calls out that if you're going after a hive-touched boy, you'll do it with his eyes on you the whole way — Hollowmoot doesn't forgive parties who bring the blight back through its gates. Sera presses her son's fishing hook into Ysolde's hands like a promise, and the causeway road toward Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple lies open ahead of you, rain-slick and waiting.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The causeway falls away behind you and the world narrows to reed and rain — chest-high stalks, black channels, and reed mats that look solid until your boot finds nothing underneath. Somewhere ahead, faint as a held breath, you can just hear it: a thin, wordless humming carried on the wind from the direction of the temple. Then the reeds part and there they are — three pilgrim-guards in oiled grey, quarterstaves crossed, standing on the one line of old pilings that doesn't want to swallow you whole. At their front, a lean woman with a temple seal at her throat looks past all of you and settles her eyes on Ysolde. "I know that face," she says. "Turn back to Hollowmoot, or give us the one the Order wants, and the rest of you may pass."

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: You know my face, Sister. Yes. But you serve the Drowned Temple, not the Order's hunters. The boy—Tomas—he followed the swarm-song here. We came to bring him back. That's temple work, and you know it.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward just enough to close the distance, rain dripping from her weathered face. She doesn't approach the crossed quarterstaves as threat—instead, she plants her weight steady on the pilings, the fishing hook Sera pressed into her hands now visible at her belt. Her eyes lock on Sister Agnet's, the same patience she once used to listen to night-barge crew members settling into their darkest fears. She's been hunted before. She doesn't run from it. She meets it.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Sister, the Order marked Ysolde for her sins, not for helping a drowning boy find his mother. I swore by these waters to cross every soul before the flood takes them—and Tomas is still singing out there. I won't turn back now, and I won't hand her over to buy passage.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps forward to stand beside Ysolde, his eyes meeting Sister Agnet's without flinching. The rain falls cold and heavy around them, and his fingers twitch—reading the pattern of water and time, the urgency that groans from the reeds. He plants his feet on the pilings, making clear with the set of his shoulders that he will not move, will not bend, and will not let her take Ysolde while breath still carries him forward.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I'm not turning back, Sister, and I'm not handing over Ysolde. A boy needs saving, and I've sworn an oath. Move.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps forward directly into the guards' path, drawing herself up tall. She summons the same iron will that turned back the hive-touched pack on the causeway, letting it fill every line of her body and every word she speaks. Her hand rises in a warding gesture as she stares directly at Sister Agnet—unmoved and unmoving—her presence alone carrying the force of her refusal. The Order trained her better than this, and she will not be stopped from a vow freely given.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: You know who I am — Captain Verrick made sure of that. I'm already marked enemy, already cast out. Take me if you want, but Ysolde passes, and so do we all. There's a boy out there who needs saving from what the swarm-song's done to him, and I didn't learn to hold the line just to abandon him.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps forward to the front of the party, placing herself between Sister Agnet and Ysolde. Her hand rests on her weapon hilt, but she's not drawing — not yet. She's simply refusing to move aside, her posture that of someone who has already chosen her ground and won't yield it. Her eyes don't waver from the temple leader's face. She invokes the truth of her own disgrace: she's already everything the Order has decided to hate, so there's nothing more they can take from her except her life.)

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: There—do you see? The temple itself sends word ahead. Let them. Every hunter the Order sends, I've already faced worse in the dark. We're not stopping for ghosts.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — attack with Will: dice - - 0 +, invoking Vowed to stand against the Wardens' torches for one more house [MO-A3], Exorcist Who Doubts the Hive Has Souls [MO-HC] → Epic (+7) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (Sister Agnet, Order Patrol Leader mild consequence)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Morwen's will breaks over Sister Agnet like the flood breaking a levee — not force of arms but force of conviction, an oath so plainly true it finds the crack beneath the woman's doctrine and drives straight through. Agnet's crossed staff wavers; for one long breath she looks less like a hunter and more like a girl who once believed the Order's mercy meant something, staggering back a step with the wind gone out of her. The two pilgrim-guards flanking her hesitate, staves half-lowered, waiting for an order that doesn't come. Behind Ysolde, Aldous, and Mire standing unmoved on the pilings, Agnet finally lowers her staff herself, jaw tight, eyes wet with something that isn't just rain. "Go, then," she says, voice rough. "Bring the boy back before the temple does what it does to the rest of them. But Ysolde — this isn't finished. The Order doesn't forget a face twice." She steps aside, and her guards part with her, leaving the old pilings clear and the path to Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple open through the rain.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The reeds give way at last to broken stone — pillars standing waist-deep in black water, a roofline collapsed into the flood, and above it all the belltower leaning drunk against the grey sky, its bell long silent but the air around it humming with that same wordless swarm-song, closer now, almost sweet. Candlelight flickers wet and orange in the temple's drowned nave, and shapes move between the pillars: pilgrims in temple grey, swaying gently in time with the song, eyes half-lidded, not quite hive-touched but not quite right either. At the base of the belltower stands a tall man in a priest's ruined vestments, waterlogged and stitched with barnacle and reed, one hand raised toward the tower as if in benediction. And far above, clinging to the bell-frame in the rain, small and pale, a boy who can only be Tomas — swaying too, humming back to the tower, one hand already dark at the knuckles with the first bloom of the hive.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Tomas! Your mother sent me—I have your hook. That song isn't yours, boy. Come down from there, and I'll take you back to Sera, I swear it.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde raises her voice through the rain and the humming, holding Sera's fishing hook high so the light catches it. She steps forward across the broken stone, moving carefully but not flinching—not attacking, just stepping into the space between the priest and the boy. Her weathered face turns up toward Tomas, and her whole posture shifts into something the night-barge crew would recognize: the listening stance, the one that says *I see you, I hear what's beneath the fear*. She keeps her hands visible, empty except for the hook, and she watches the Drowned Priest's face as she speaks, reading what moves in that waterlogged ruin of a man.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The rain shows me the boy isn't gone yet—his mother's tears still reach him through the water. There's still a thread between them, still something that answers to his name.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous closes his eyes and lets the rain fall heavy across his face. His fingers twitch in the familiar pattern of reading water-signs—tracing the temperature shifts, the current's whisper, the echo of movements only a drowned man could know. The ghosts that mark him shudder and point toward the boy above, and when Aldous opens his eyes again they're sharp with certainty, reading not just the hive-song but the fragile thread of love still holding Tomas to his mother's name.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: That thing is calling my boy down into the rot. Not today—I'm binding you to the water and breaking your claim on every soul in this temple.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen strides forward across the broken pillars without hesitation, rain streaming down her face. She draws deep on the exorcist's will the Order drilled into her, speaking words of binding with absolute conviction as she locks her gaze on the ruined priest and reaches out to sever the connection holding Tomas to the bell-frame.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: The priest's holding the song with everything he has—see how he's fixed on that tower? We might have a moment while his attention's on Tomas, not on us.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps carefully onto the broken temple stones, her trained eyes tracking the priest's movements. She watches how his upraised hand guides the swarm-song like a conductor drawing notes from an instrument, sees the pilgrims' swaying rhythm matched perfectly to the melody. For just a moment, while his attention is completely fixed on Tomas in the belltower, the rest of them might move unnoticed.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Yes, Drowned Father. I swear it by the water that marks me—I mean to bring the boy down from your mercy and return him to his mother's name. That's my oath, and I won't speak false to you.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — create advantage with Notice: dice - 0 + 0 → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — attack with Will: dice - - - -, invoking Exorcist Who Doubts the Hive Has Souls [MO-HC], Vowed to stand against the Wardens' torches for one more house [MO-A3] → Great (+4) vs Great (+4): TIE

transcript.speaker: Table

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Swaying Pilgrim-Flock attacks Ysolde (mental): Mediocre (+0) vs Ysolde's Will Abysmal (-3) — hit for 3

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Morwen's binding words strike true and the priest staggers, his grip on the bell-song fraying for an instant — but the backlash of severing that much devotion floods back through her own outstretched hand, and his ruined face snaps down from the tower to fix on her instead. The Priest's Attention Fixed on the Tower breaks; now he knows exactly who's fighting him, and the swaying pilgrims begin to turn toward Morwen too.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Aldous's ghosts don't lie: he sees it now, plain as a lit lamp in the dark — a thread of love still runs from Tomas straight back to Sera's grief, thin as spider-silk but unbroken. That thread is a door, if someone can reach it. Mire, meanwhile, reads the priest like a tide table — his whole being poured into the tower, into the boy, into the song — and for one perfect heartbeat the rest of you are ghosts he can't see. Morwen seizes that heartbeat and drives her will into him like a spike, and it *works* — his grip on Tomas shudders, the humming stutters — but the cost is immediate: severing that much devotion floods backward through her own outstretched hand, and the priest's ruined face snaps away from the belltower to fix, hard and furious, on her. The opening Mire bought slams shut the instant it opens; he knows exactly who's fighting him now, and so do the swaying pilgrims, their half-lidded eyes all turning toward Morwen like a tide reversing. In the same breath, the flock's massed hum surges and crashes into Ysolde where she stands closest to the boy — not sound but *pressure*, words that aren't words pushing into the cracks of her thoughts. She staggers under it, teeth gritted, forcing the noise back behind gritted resolve, but it costs her — the weight of it settles into her mind like water finding a crack, and she can feel it there still, humming, unwilling to fully leave.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Tomas! Your mother's grief sings louder than any hive-song. That thread between you and Sera—I hear it, and it's unbreakable. Come down to her name, not to the dark.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde plants her feet on the broken temple stone, rain streaming down her weathered face. She raises Sera's fishing hook like a beacon, an anchor—and she doesn't attack the Priest with force, but with the deep listening that once made her dangerous to the Order. She opens herself completely, invokes the truth of who she is: the Cook of the Night-Barge Who Hears Everything. She reaches past the Priest's ceremony, past the humming still clawing at her own mind, and she *calls* to Tomas—not with commands, but with the patient understanding that cuts through every wall. She's offering him a thread back to his mother's love, stronger and truer than the hive's pull.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Tomas! The thread your mother wove—it still holds through water and song both. Come back to Sera, boy. Come back to her name.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous raises his hands toward the belltower, fingers spread as if cradling something impossibly fragile. Invoking the connection that still holds—The Boy's Thread—the rain falls heavier around him, carrying Sera's tears mixed with the flood's cold. He traces that invisible bond through the water itself, and his voice rises clear and strong, speaking Tomas's name like a summons the boy cannot refuse. The ghosts that mark him press close, drowned things that know the pull of love better than the pull of song, and they lend their weight to his reaching.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I felt that break, priest. I'm finishing this—you don't own these people.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen surges forward across the broken pillars without hesitation, reaching out toward the ruined priest. She pours everything into the connection she just shattered—her exorcist's will, her oath unbroken—driving deeper to sever it completely this time. The rain runs down her face as she leans into the assault, refusing to yield an inch.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Fall back—they're turning on Morwen. I'll hold them here.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire plants herself between the swaying pilgrims and Morwen, weapon drawn, moving into the stance that held Wick Lane a hundred nights—feet set, shoulders square, eyes reading every hypnotic sway and half-lidded turn. She's held worse than this. She's held the line when everything else was breaking. Her blade comes up steady, not to kill but to drive them back, to say with every inch of iron and will: you do not pass. Not while she's still standing.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — attack with Empathy: dice - - 0 -, invoking Exiled Cook of the Night-Barge Who Hears Everything [YS-HC], The Boy's Thread [A-1.4.2] → Superb (+5) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS (The Drowned Priest stress 2)

transcript.text: Aldous — overcome with Empathy: dice + 0 0 + → Superb (+5) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The four of you move as one current against the drowned man's will. Ysolde's voice — patient, unbreakable, the same listening that once held a dying barge crew together — finds the thread Aldous traced and pours down it whole: *Sera's grief, Sera's love, stronger than any song.* The Priest reels back against the tower stone, his raised hand faltering, and above him Tomas's head snaps up — really up, eyes clearing for the first time in three nights — his small fingers scrabbling at the bell-frame as the humming in his own throat stutters into silence. Morwen doesn't let the opening close twice; she drives her will home a second time, and this time the binding doesn't just fray — it snaps, and the Priest goes down hard against a broken pillar, coughing water, his authority over the tower shattered along with his composure. Around Mire, the swaying pilgrims who turned to answer Morwen's assault stagger instead as her blade and her stance break their rhythm, blinking like sleepers waking mid-stride, the trance-glaze draining out of their faces one by one. High above, Tomas begins to climb down — slow, shaking, but climbing, toward the fishing hook Ysolde still holds high and the mother's name Aldous spoke into the rain. It isn't clean: the dark bloom at his knuckles hasn't gone, and won't — the hive has him marked even freed. But he's *himself*, crying and terrified and calling for his mother, dropping the last few feet into Mire's steadying arms as the Priest, robbed of his flock's attention and his hold on the boy both, drags himself upright and back into the drowned nave, snarling something about the tower not forgetting this. The swarm-song does not resume. Rain falls into sudden, ringing quiet.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The quiet doesn't last. From the drowned nave the Priest's voice rises again, cracked and furious, no longer a song but a summons — and out past the broken pillars, back toward the reed-choked causeway, something answers: a ragged chorus of wet, tuneless humming, closer than it should be, moving fast. Tomas flinches hard against Mire's shoulder at the sound, whispering that they took his friend Wik the same way, that the ones outside don't stop, don't feel the spears go in. The floodwater around the pillars is already climbing past your ankles again, swallowing the safe stones you crossed to get in, and the only dry line back toward Hollowmoot runs straight through the reeds where that humming is gathering. The Priest, dragging himself upright against the drowned altar, manages one last ruined smile: "The tower calls its own home. Let's see if you can outrun the flood and the flock both."

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: I hear the pattern—when it pauses, we move. Listening taught me to hear anything.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde closes her eyes as the Hive-Touched Pack's humming rises from the reeds. She tilts her face toward the sound, settling into the listening stance that held her dying night-barge crew together in darkness. She reads the swarm-pulse like water, finding the rhythm, the moments when it breaks and gaps open. Invoking the Cook of the Night-Barge Who Hears Everything [YS-HC], her fingers twitch, marking the path through.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The rain shows me a way through — there's a thread of current that knows the deep stones, and my ghosts remember every ford in Sallowmere. We follow that thread now, before the flock closes in.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous closes his eyes as rain streams down his face, fingers twitching through the familiar water-reading gesture. The drowned voices that mark him press close and whisper urgent directions — he can see the current's true shape now, the stone spine beneath the flood that will hold the group's weight if they move fast. When his eyes snap open, they're sharp with certainty. He points toward the path only someone marked by drowning could read, one hand reaching back toward the others.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: You're done here, Priest. No more songs, no more claims. This ends now.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen strides forward through the rising water without hesitation, her jaw set, eyes blazing. She reaches out with both hands and speaks words of binding—the same iron-hard exorcist's will that broke his hold on Tomas, poured into one final severing strike. She's finishing this before his pack arrives, before he can summon anything else. The Order trained her for this.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Your summoning ends here, priest. Not today.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire shifts Tomas securely to one side, bracing him tight against her body. She never breaks her focus from the priest struggling upright against the altar—he's spent, wounded by Morwen's binding, but still dangerous. Still summoning. She's held Wick Lane against odds like this a hundred nights. She closes the distance across the broken temple stones with the steady, relentless purpose of someone who knows how to hold the line: step by step, blade up, no hesitation.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: You don't summon another soul while I'm breathing, priest. Not one more.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire accepts a compel.

transcript.text: Morwen — attack with Will: dice + 0 - 0 → Great (+4) vs Mediocre (+0): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (The Drowned Priest taken out)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — attack with Fight: dice + 0 - - → Good (+3) vs Mediocre (+0): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (The Drowned Priest mild consequence)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Morwen's second strike doesn't just break the Priest's hold — it breaks him. The binding closes like a fist around everything that was ever holy in him, and he goes down in the flooded nave with a sound like a man drowning twice, hands scrabbling uselessly at the altar stone. Mire is on him before he can rise again, blade flat against his throat, and whatever fight was left in the Drowned Priest empties out of him into the black water. He doesn't move. Behind you, the humming chorus in the reeds is close now — close enough to hear the wet click of hooked spears — but Ysolde has already found the rhythm of it, the gaps where the swarm-song stutters and leaves a blind moment, and Aldous has already read the old stone spine beneath the flood that the pack won't know to follow. "Now," Ysolde says, and you move — not toward the reeds where the humming gathers, but along the hidden line Aldous traced, Tomas clutched tight against Mire's shoulder, the drowned temple and its silenced priest falling away behind you into the rain. The pack's cry rises in fury when it finds the nave empty, but by then you're already ankle-deep on the old pilings, and Hollowmoot's lights are a promise on the grey horizon ahead.

costs.text: The moment Mire spots Scarhook's scarred face among the pack — the same man who once wore a Warden's cloak beside her — the old fury rises. She wants to break off her survey of the ford and go for him instead, leaving the party blind to what lies ahead.

Sergeant Coale's eyes narrow in recognition as you comfort the mother — 'You're the exorcist from the Orrin trials, aren't you?' he says loud enough for the whole crowd to hear, and suddenly every frightened face in the square is staring at Morwen instead of Sera, murmuring her name, some reaching t

A hooded figure at the edge of the crowd — grey robes half-hidden under a fisherman's cloak — goes very still at the sound of Ysolde's voice, then turns and slips away toward the gate, moving with the unhurried purpose of someone who has somewhere urgent to report.

Sister Agnet's eyes never leave Ysolde even as Morwen presses her — she signals one of the pilgrim-guards to peel off and start back toward the temple road, clearly meaning to send word ahead that the marked woman is here, whatever happens in this standoff.

The Drowned Priest's ruined face turns from the belltower toward Aldous — the only one of you he seems to truly see — and asks, in a voice like water through a drowned throat, whether he means to steal the boy from the hive's mercy. Bound by his oath, Aldous cannot lie, and the truth spills out of h

Morwen's binding words strike true and the priest staggers, his grip on the bell-song fraying for an instant — but the backlash of severing that much devotion floods back through her own outstretched hand, and his ruined face snaps down from the tower to fix on her instead. The Priest's Attention Fi
Mire is so fixed on finishing the priest that she pushes deeper into striking range than is safe with Tomas braced against her — if the blow doesn't land clean, the boy is exposed.

free_text.best_moment: When I used my listening to read both Sera's raw, desperate grief AND the swarm-song's rhythm at the same time—my core character trait became the literal, mechanical solution to saving Tomas. It felt like everything the night-barge crew taught me had shaped me into exactly the person this moment needed. That's when Ysolde mattered most.
free_text.most_frustrating: When the Priest's attention fixed on Morwen and I felt like I should have been able to do something more direct to defend her or break that hold—but the fictional moment had already moved past it. I wanted one more action to stand beside her in that surge forward.
free_text.background_used: Good. The Night-barge Cook Who Hears Everything wasn't used as flavor—it was used as the functional, mechanical core of solving the crisis. Sera came to me because I listen. I found the path through the swarm-song because I listen. That felt like true character integration, not just backstory window-dressing.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to do something more active and specific with Sera's fishing hook beyond just holding it as a symbol. I also wanted at least one moment where I directly attacked or confronted the Drowned Priest myself, rather than always supporting others' strikes.
free_text.one_sentence: Ysolde's defining trait—that she hears everything—was treated not as a passive flavor point but as the story's solution, and that felt like being truly seen.

free_text.best_moment: Aldous reading the invisible thread between Tomas and his mother through rain-sight and drowned-ghost whispers, then speaking the boy's name as a summons—it wove together all of his core abilities and felt like the true turning point of the rescue.
free_text.most_frustrating: The Drowned Priest moved quickly into combat before there was real space to negotiate or understand what drew him to claim these souls—but that's how the narrative momentum required things to go, and the victory was satisfying regardless.
free_text.background_used: Nearly every thread: the vow to cross souls shaped the entire mission, the rain-reading gift enabled critical successes, the mark from drowned ghosts was essential to understanding Tomas, and the Cannot Lie to a Priest trouble created a genuine oath-moment. None of it felt forced—it was woven naturally into the GM's world. This landed very well.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: A real conversation with the Drowned Priest to understand what need or hunger drove him to summon souls—I wanted to engage with him as something more than an obstacle. Though I recognize the rescue had its own urgency.
free_text.one_sentence: Your vow to cross every soul felt genuinely vital to this story's resolution, and your connection to drowned things shaped not just how you won but why you were the one who could.

free_text.best_moment: Breaking the Drowned Priest's hold on Tomas the second time with that Success with Style on Will. It felt like everything Morwen is built for clicking into place at exactly the right moment—the oath, the exorcist's conviction, the stakes all crystallizing at once. That was satisfying.
free_text.most_frustrating: My character's core doubt—that I'm not sure the hive has souls—never really came into play. The Priest would have been perfect to explore that with, but we stayed in straightforward rescue/combat mode instead. Also my trouble "Too Famous to Hide" was set up beautifully at the causeway gate but then barely materialized as actual problem.
free_text.background_used: My oath aspect got genuine weight—it became the keystone to standing down Sister Agnet, and that landed well. My high concept as Exorcist worked throughout. But the *doubt* buried in that concept, the meat of who Morwen actually is, didn't get much air. Unfair is too strong; I'd say it was used partially—the surface, not the depth.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted a moment where Morwen had to actually wrestle with her doubt. The Priest summoning his flock and claiming the hive's love was genuine could have been that—a moment to question if she was doing the right thing, not just the strong thing. Instead it stayed in the combat register.
free_text.one_sentence: Morwen got to be effective and central, but the actual complexity of her doubt was left on the table.

free_text.best_moment: Stepping forward to Sister Agnet and claiming her own disgrace as unbreakable ground—the moment where being marked enemy became an asset instead of a liability, and Mire refused to be moved by threats that had already landed.
free_text.most_frustrating: Never quite getting to understand the Drowned Priest—who he was before, what he wanted beyond the hive's pull, whether there was anything left to save. We defeated him but didn't know him.
free_text.background_used: Extensively. Captain Verrick's vendetta, Wick Lane, being marked enemy of the Causeway Wardens—all of it came alive in how NPCs recognized and reacted to Mire. It landed well, integrated naturally rather than forced.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to dig deeper into Hollowmoot's politics through Contacts, or figure out more about what the Warden sergeant was actually hunting. The session was perfectly paced for action but left some investigative threads dangling.
free_text.one_sentence: Mire's backstory was woven through the whole session and made her central to it—her history wasn't just flavor, it shaped what she could and couldn't do, and what she had to stand firm on.

chronicle.summary: The party faced down the Order's patrol on the pilings, let Morwen's iron conviction turn Sister Agnet aside, and pushed on into Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple to find Tomas trance-bound in the flooded belltower. Through combined will, empathy, and read-water instinct, they severed the Drowned Priest's hold on the swarm-song, pulled the boy back to his mother's name, and beat the Priest down and out when he tried to summon the Hive-Touched Pack against them. They escaped along a hidden stone spine only Aldous could read, slipping past the closing pack and back toward Hollowmoot's lights with Tomas alive, marked, but free.
